topic.title: Git Client Add-on
topic.shortdesc: The Git Client add-on integrates a full Git client into , enabling you to commit, push, pull, branch, and resolve conflicts without leaving the editor.

body.p: The Git Client add-on contributes a built-in Git client directly in . After you install the add-on, you can use the top-level Git menu, three dedicated views, a preferences page, and contextual Git actions in other views and editors.

The sections that follow guide you through the full Git Client setup and workflow. Install the add-on and configure access first, set up a repository, then use the workflow sections to review, stage, commit, push, pull, manage branches, and resolve conflicts. The add-on also uses the comparison and merge tools available in . After the workflow topics, the interface overview and action reference provide lookup information.

section.title: Workflow Overview
section.p: The Git Client add-on works with a selected Git working copy. It shows local file changes, staged changes, branch state, and repository history so you can complete common Git tasks without leaving . The overview below describes the main flow covered in this chapter.

After the add-on is installed and connected to the repositories you need, a common workflow includes these actions:
Select an existing working copy or clone a repository.
Review the files that changed in the working copy.
Compare changes before you include them in a commit.
Stage the files or parts of files that belong in the next commit.
Commit the staged changes with a clear message.
Pull changes from the remote repository and push your local commits.
Resolve conflicts only when Git reports them.
The next sections first cover installation and access, then move through repository setup and the daily Git workflows. Interface and action reference topics are available after the workflow sections.
